reason: The user directed that MTP0 on the row-invariant kernel is publishable on its own if it passes every determinism test, independent of MTP1. R147 ran the 100-300-token repeat probe and the c1-c64 identity ladder on MTP1 servers only; this amendment runs both on MTP0 servers of the same image so the MTP0 claim rests on MTP0 evidence.
run_order: preflight as R147 (clean journal, both devices normal, compute and XCCL health, zero lane containers)
mtp0-c: third same-image MTP0 strict server, empty cache, pre-canaries, strict natural-512 suite with post-canaries, then the medium-prefill repeat probe on the same server, graceful stop, postflight

ladder-mtp0: MTP0 server in the frozen R63 configuration; harness regenerates 64 sequential oracles then measures c1,2,4,8,16,32,64 with repeats=1, max_tokens=128, ignore_eos, temperature 0, --return-token-ids --require-output-identity; graceful stop; postflight

gates.G1c: mtp0-c vs R147 mtp0-a 12/12 complete arrays (third independent MTP0 server)
gates.G4c: 12 rows, natural EOS, zero cached tokens, canaries before and after, realistic_final_gate passed
gates.G5(mtp0): at 100, 168, 200, 224, 250, 300 prompt tokens x5 repeats: one token-ID stream, one token-logprob array, one top-logprob array, zero cached tokens
gates.G6(mtp0): every complete concurrent output at c1..c64 equals its sequential oracle; harness exit 0
gates.mtp0_determinism_qualified: G1c, G4c, G5(mtp0), G6(mtp0) all pass together with R147 G1

abort_conditions: as R147: any fault signature, non-normal device, health failure, image mismatch, or a server that does not reach health in 45 minutes
on_pass: MTP0 on the R139 image is determinism-qualified for c1-c64 identity and 100-300-token repeat exactness at the endpoint; write the note and present the publication text change for the user's approval (the README/package edit itself follows lab rules: strict gates passed, numbers from this clean boot)
on_failure: record which MTP0 gate failed; the MTP0 claim is not made
